sourceInformation.source: Turtles (1983 US Odyssey² release); arcade ancestor Konami, 1981
sourceInformation.tech: JavaScript, HTML, Web Audio; my-3D2dge v0.89.1 (8ecc2f6) with local Shell hidden-setting extension; AI Hub client 1.4.0 / Session Protocol v1 (35a1047), unmodified
sourceInformation.artDirection: Original shaded pixel art: warm miniature hotel, patterned turtle shells, expressive hatchlings and distinct beetle silhouettes
sourceInformation.animation: Native continuous E.Blob rig clocks/springs with custom anatomy, gait, easing, event poses, native particles and sorted actors
sourceInformation.audio: Original code-synthesized music, sound effects and formant-filtered gibberish voices; music defaults to 10%; no audio files
sourceInformation.online: AI Hub authoritative shared-world co-op for 1–2 players, including dedicated hosts; standalone solo and simultaneous local co-op
sourceInformation.testing: Headless rules, input-driven campaign bots, native engine stepping, browser automation, emulated gamepads/touch, two-page Hub harness, generated audio signal analysis; no physical hardware or human listening
sourceInformation.research: US manual text and rendered pictures; documented Odyssey² gameplay screenshots; release entry and historical review. No gameplay recording watched or audio heard.

testingFeedback: 17 unique game, UI and integration issues found and fixed; test-harness false positives are excluded. Details and covering checks are in docs/validation.md.
1 critical remote-seat input lock, reproduced after a long packet gap with advancing action counters; fixed. No unresolved critical issues.

The exact exported HTML campaign driven through native keyboard actions: all 26 rescues, 2 lives left, 15400 points, bombs/refill/damage/recovery and all pursuit states exercised. Real Hub client/bridge campaigns also won with player and dedicated hosts.

The initial generic export regex: it matched harmless interview text and .wave properties rather than runtime imports or audio files. It was replaced with targeted packaging checks and actual file:// request evidence.
engineFeedback: Native shaded pixel drawing, TileMap/Grid navigation, continuous rig timing, synthesized audio, standard controller-accessible screens and exact headless stepping form a coherent foundation.

Yes. Keeping a GridMover direction queued in flight initially skipped enemy junction decisions. Input.feed simulates gestures, so real touch pointers were needed to test the invisible stick. Both assumptions were corrected.
A deterministic simultaneous rescue simulation with passengers, reserved homes, team resources, pursuit and an authoritative shared-world network adapter.
Combining buffered movement, immediate reversal, explicit device seats and snapshot reconciliation while preserving the native renderer and menu behavior.

Added a hidden:true setting flag to the native Shell catalogue filter. Developer sliders still use native controls on explicit developer pages, while ordinary Settings and production Hub sessions do not expose them.
A native simultaneous-seat arcade shell and a documented custom-creature rig base would reduce integration work.
promptFeedback: The explicit rescue loop, campaign lessons, and evidence requirements made the intended finished game clear.
The source year covers several ports; PLAN.md resolves this to the US Odyssey² hotel release.
Keeping deterministic rescue rules consistent across local co-op, dedicated Hub hosts, prediction, presentation, and a single-file export.
Provide a small engine-native shared-world rescue example and a compact acceptance checklist alongside the detailed plan.

aiHub.name: Turtle Shell Service
aiHub.description: Check in to a beetle-bothered hotel and carry its tiny turtle guests home. Five floors of clever escapes, scarce bug bombs, and cooperative shell service lead to a rooftop reunion.
aiHub.controls: WASD/arrows or left stick/D-pad move; Space/Cross bug bomb; click to walk; drag touch with assisted POP; local P2 arrows/Right Shift.
